mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand as measured by HOUST coincides with stronger S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased market optimism about corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Over 20-day walk-forward, 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment as indicated by PAYEMS leads to higher consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes with high unemployment, 20-day returns are negative despite PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4%, the tightening bias increases discount rates, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 12 such events, 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand or supply chain issues, which typically precede short-term S&P 500 declines.
failure_condition: During periods of rising INDPRO, 5-day returns are positive and statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising RSAFS (retail sales) indicate strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive in 80% of such RSAFS-up periods (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in UNRATE above 4% signals labor market tightening that reduces corporate profit expectations and causes negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In >50% of UNRATE > 4% regimes, 20-day returns are non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between falling CPIAUCSL (inflation) and rising FEDFUNDS creates a disinflationary momentum that drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return when the two proxies move in opposite directions in other regimes.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (evidenced by a one-standard-deviation drop in GDPC1), S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 20 days as market anticipates slower growth.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative in >70% of such events (binomial test).
